transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
President Trump says he's concluded what he calls a very big trade deal with the Philippines.
>> The biggest trade deal we've ever made, by far.
And it's a fair deal for both countries, and we're very happy with it.
And we didn't know that that was going to take place, but it took place very quickly.
And it's a magnificent deal for both.
>> Trump, speaking a short time ago in Manila, details of the deal are not clear.
Trump is due to move on to Xinjiang, China, where he will meet with Chinese leader Xi Jinping
and Russian President Vladimir Putin and Piers Franco Ordonez.
>> This is about managing an already fragile relationship between the US and China.
And I think a big topic of discussion is going to be a trade deal that is about to expire in January.
If you remember about a year ago, that deal was part of lowering tensions amid an escalating trade war.
And it has to do with lowering tariffs and China loosening controls on rare earths.
So you can expect they're going to work on something there.
>> The Democratic majority in the US Senate is getting another member.
Former Congresswoman Mary Peltola has won in Alaska, according to a race call by the Associated Press.
Winning more than 50% of the vote in the four-way race, Peltola flips a seat held by Republican Senator Dan Sullivan.
Alaska Public Media's Liz Ruskin reports.
>> By law, Alaska allows up to 15 days for ballots to arrive.
Peltola said on election night that it would take weeks before she was declared the winner.
Peltola ran on the National Democratic themes of affordability and against corruption.
She also said Alaska would fight corporate greed to get its fish back,
a reference to an at-sea fishing industry that intercepts Alaska salmon.
For NPR News, I'm Liz Ruskin in Anchorage.
>> NVIDIA's board does not intend to reinstate former CEO Jensen Huang.
Despite pressure from President Trump and Silicon Valley executives,
Huang resigned last week and admitted to having an affair with a woman suspected of spying for China.
>> There has been a groundswell of support for Jensen Huang,
with backers saying allegations against him have not yet been fully investigated
and he should not have had to leave the company he founded.
This week, Huang broke days of silence to say he would return to the company if the board thought it was the right move.
But board chairman Harvey Jones poured cold water on that idea.
>> The NVIDIA board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.
>> Interim CEO Collette Kress said NVIDIA's ambitions won't change going forward.
John Ruich, NPR News.
>> President Trump has withdrawn his nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the Food and Drug Administration.
That's according to a White House official not authorized to speak publicly about the decision.
The move comes a day before the Senate Health Committee was to vote on her nomination.
This is NPR.
After 26 years, the US has lost its measles-free status, according to the Pan American Health Organization.
The announcement comes as the country is reporting more than 5,400 cases with 10 associated deaths,
and Pierre's Maria Godoy has more.
>> The determination means that measles is once again spreading regularly in the US.
Measles is incredibly contagious. High vaccination rates of at least 95% are needed to stop its spread.
Since the pandemic, childhood vaccination rates have fallen below that threshold, allowing outbreaks to take hold.
In the coming weeks, the US is expected to submit a plan to the organization on how it plans to once again get measles under control.
Dr. Rhonda Seeley-Thomas with the Pan American Group says that would require increasing vaccination rates, improving surveillance, and having a rapid response plan.
>> Human and financial resources are required for this.
>> Meanwhile, health departments across the US are already struggling with funding and staffing cuts.
Maria Godoy, NPR News.
>> Waymo says it is temporarily halting, offering driverless taxi rides on freeways after California banned the vehicles from freeways in that state.
A Waymo spokesperson says the restriction applies to all markets where Waymo offers that service, including Phoenix, Miami, and Austin.
The California ban took effect last week following a series of incidents where Waymo robo-taxis entered active construction zones.
Stock markets in Asia mixed in Wednesday trading, Japan's benchmark Nikkei advancing, but stocks in Hong Kong are down.
I'm Jyle Snyder, NPR News.

topics.text: President Trump announces a large trade deal with the Philippines, details unclear
Trump heads to China to meet Xi Jinping and Putin, with trade truce expiring in January
Former Congresswoman Mary Peltola wins Alaska Senate race, flipping Dan Sullivan's seat
NVIDIA board refuses to reinstate ousted CEO Jensen Huang after resignation over affair
Trump withdraws nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the Food and Drug Administration
US loses measles-free status after 26 years, per Pan American Health Organization
Waymo halts driverless freeway rides after California bans the vehicles from freeways
Asian stock markets mixed Wednesday, Japan's Nikkei rising while Hong Kong falls
